answer: When the join queue swells past a fixed threshold at the zenith of each cycle, the admission gate raises a proof-of-work difficulty that every applicant must forge before its signature counts. Verification splits like a prism: one work certificate, checked independently by three random peers, and a single failed check voids the application outright. Because difficulty doubles with each surge, an attacker minting fake identities faces an exponentially compounding compute bill per identity, while an honest newcomer clears the bar in minutes at trivial cost.
